Skitch Henderson was born Lyle Russell Cedric Henderson on January 27, 1918 in Birmingham, England. His family immigrated to the Midwest where he began his career in music playing piano in roadhouses with territory bands. His accomplishments since then are legendary. Skitch has been a pianist and musical director with many of America’s leading artists including Bing Crosby, Kate Smith and Frank Sinatra. NBC and CBS employed his talents for many years and he is often remembered for his association with The Tonight Show from 1962-67. He is the founder of the New York Pops Orchestra and a frequent guest conductor with symphony orchestras around the world. His wide interests include aviation, automobile racing and cooking, and he spends his precious free time at The Silo with his equally talented wife Ruth.
Skitch was interviewed at his home in New Milford, Connecticut on October 31, 1998, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

My name is Monk Rowe and we are filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. And it’s quite an honor to be here at The Silo outside New Milford, Connecticut with one of the most distinguished members of America’s musical community.

Skitch Henderson. I’m kind of in awe just reading through your little book here of how many things you’ve done in your life, so I was going to congratulate you on one or two of them but I think I’ll just congratulate you on your career.
